title: Benny Carter's band walks out of the Plantation
summary: A white patron hits Benny Carter's trombonist, J. J. Johnson, Carter pulls his band out, and George Hudson's band fills in.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Because -- I said Benny Carter was in there, because there was some kind of (unintelligible) wasn't there?

See, that was a package. Now, they might have paid $4,000 for that package, see. It was a package deal. Benny Carter's band, and he had J.J. on the trombone at the time, see. And what happened, J.J. had been laughing at this girl, or something back there, and one of the boys back there, one of the white fellows, hit him. And Benny Carter pulled his band out. Well, they didn't have a band to play. They went and got George Hudson, and George Hudson agreed to go in there and play. All the other bands wouldn't go back there and play, wouldn't play in there. That's what happened.
